This elective is intended to provide medical students with experiential learning in medical education, curriculum development, and change management, as they actively participate in the MedEdMorphosis process (https://pulse.utah.edu/site/MedEdMorphosis). Students will learn about and apply medical education theories and principles as they partner with other students, staff, faculty, and community partners to identify issues, generate ideas, design programs, and manage implementation of change. The experiences gained through the elective will be particularly beneficial to students who have interest in academic medicine and medical education. Students will be able to tailor the participation in the elective to their needs and interests via a rolling credits system based on level of involvement in MedEdMorphosis activities. Students can opt to receive either non-clinical or clinical credit, based on the primary focus their participation. For example, participating mostly in MD Program Implementation activities, especially in Phase 1, such as helping pilot PBL or design assessments would merit non-clinical credit, while helping pilot student-led clinic operations would merit clinical credit. At the time you seek permission to enroll, be prepared to identify the amount and type of credit you would like to receive.

The Medical Students as Teachers elective prepares medical students to become effective teachers for their residency and beyond by participating in one of the UUSOM preclinical or clinical courses in an instructional role. Students will receive didactic instruction from educational experts on learning objectives, pedagogy, assessment, feedback, and evaluation. Students will apply knowledge and skills gained from didactics and reading to take part in structured and monitored teaching activities. The type of teaching project will be determined by a student's individual learning plan and area of interest (e.g., teaching at the bedside/in clinic, teaching in small group, teaching in large group, etc.). Students will receive guidance and feedback on their teaching project from a UUSOM faculty mentor.

The Students as Teachers Pathway I course will serve as the introductory course for first year medical students interested in participating in the Students as Teachers (SaT) Pathway. The course will help students determine whether the SaT pathway is the good fit for them and will provide a foundation in topics including: the role physicians play as educators for patients and the community, medical literacy, the unique role of residents as teachers, characteristics of effective feedback, and the variety of careers available in medical education.

The Students as Teachers Pathway II course will build upon knowledge gained in the Students as Teachers Pathway I course for first year medical students interested in participating in the Students as Teachers (SaT) Pathway. The course will provide a foundation in topics including: creating a positive learning climate, creating goals and objectives, basics of lesson planning and implementing lesson plans & teaching sessions.

The Students as Teachers Pathway 3 will serve as continuation for session content delivered during SaT Pathways 1&2. The course will build on teaching skills incorporated during the preceding pathway sessions, and will focus on more advanced topics in education including medical education research, presenting effective ‘chalk talks’, assessment and evaluation and role-modeling in education in the clinical setting.

The Students as Teachers Pathway 4 will build upon content delivered during SaT Pathway courses 1, 2, and 3 and lay the groundwork for clinical education techniques that students will experience in their 3rd year of medical school. They will also develop fundamental skills to help successfully educate their peers during clinical rotations.

The Students as Teachers Pathway 5 will serve as continuation for session content delivered during SaT Pathways 1-4. The course will build on teaching skills incorporated during the preceding pathway sessions, and will focus on more advanced topics in education as they present in the clinical setting while on clerkships.

The Students as Teachers Pathway 6 will serve as continuation for session content delivered during SaT Pathways 1-5. It will be a longitudinal course that will span the MS4 year, with 2 sessions in the fall and 2 in the spring taking place in the early evening to help accommodate clinical schedules. The course will build on teaching skills incorporated during the preceding pathway sessions, and will focus on more advanced topics in education and navigating a career in medical education, and will culminate in presentations of completed Capstone projects. During the course, participation in a structured teaching elective or the Getting Your Ed in the Game: Student Participation in the MedEdMorphosis Change Initiative elective is strongly encouraged. Based on the preferences of enrolled students, session will be live or via Zoom. Zoom sessions will be recorded for asynchronous availability.

All phase 3 students will complete 1 credit of near peer teaching and mentoring.  Students are expected to complete 1 credit (approximately 40 hours) of teaching and mentoring experiences.  They will be able to choose from a variety of offerings such as teaching assistant, mentoring of junior students in student led clinic or leading learning sessions during intersessions. This course will consist of experiential learning with application and reflection. In addition, students will complete knowledge modules specific to their experience and be expected to reflect on their experience at the close the course.

All students of the new MD program will participate in monthly Academic Half-Days and a Fall and Spring Intersession during Phase 3a.  Content will focus on knowledge, skills and attitudes required of all physicians, including professional identify formation, preparation for residency applications and core pillar content. Academic Half-Days will be held one afternoon each month.  The Fall and Spring Intersessions will be held during a 5-day interval between block rotations. Learning methods will include house and learning community activities, large and small group sessions, simulations and selective experiences. Of note, some monthly academic half-days may be conducted remotely.

Medical School Admissions Experience (MSAE) MD ID 7240 is an asynchronous (100% online) elective offered during the 4th year of medical school. This course will guide medical students to understand the theory and practice of admissions and to further develop leadership and organizational skills. Medical students can use this gained knowledge during the residency application process, as well as for future leadership positions. Such information and training will also be beneficial to preparing for and thriving in diverse organizations as a higher education leader within academic medicine.

Personalized Health Care is the tailoring of medical treatment to the individual characteristics of each patient. This course will review the fundamental elements of Personalized Health Care, discuss relevant case studies of preventative and therapeutic applications of Personalized Health Care, and explore future developments. Students will also have the opportunity to devise ways in which Personalized Health Care can be advanced locally, nationally, and globally.

Genetics and Medicine: Ethical, Legal and Social Issues is designed to immerse students in the emerging ethical, legal, and social issues facing the field of genetics and medicine. This is a semester-long, weekly course that meets for 13, two hour sessions. The course offers a mix of didactic content, case studies, and small group activities. This course is intended for students with graduate standing and is targeted toward students who have at least some background in human genetics and research methods. This course is mandatory for trainees in the Genomic Medicine T32 training program; students in other graduate degree programs are welcome to participate.
The Personalized Medicine Capstone project is a requirement for the Certificate in Personalized Health Care. For further information, contact the instructor.

This course will introduce students to the health issues affecting transgender patients. Through lectures, clinical exposure, and community opportunities, the students will explore discrimination issues, social and legal challenges, primary care and transgender specific care including surgery, and specific challenges related to the pediatric and adolescent transgender population. This will be structured as a continuity course, which will be spread over a full academic year in order to maximize clinical exposure in this multidisciplinary field.

The Transition to Internship course is a required capstone course for graduating senior medical students. The primary goal of the course is to prepare students to successfully transition to their matched internship.

Phase 2 Longitudinal encompasses the academic half-day program, course director meetings, the LIC theme-based scholarly project, amongst other tasks. - The academic half-day is a 4 hour per week didactic course covering content relevant to foundational and clinical sciences. - Course Director meetings occur quarterly between the LIC Director and student to discuss progress in their clinical course work, and goal setting for successful completion of their courses. - Each student will complete a longitudinal scholarly project related to the theme associated with their LIC.

This course is designed to allow medical students to learn with and from each-other. It provide opportunities for students to interact with peers from different cohorts & build community. Activities include: presentation of scholarly projects, peer-to-peer support of clinical skills development, narrative medicine & reflection on educational materials.

This course will integrate core foundational science and clinical care principles related to prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of cancer. The course will use a blend of classroom-based discussion, literature review, journal club, and clinical question-based research activities to explore foundational science concepts and patient narratives of cancer experience in depth. In addition to classroom-based activities, students will rotate in varied clinical settings to participate in clinical care for patients with cancer or suspected cancer, with a focus on asking and answering clinical questions based in foundational science concepts that explain cancer biology and treatment. Clinical settings may be outpatient and/or inpatient; specialties may include but are not limited to hematology/oncology, bone marrow transplant, radiation oncology, surgical oncology, pathology, palliative care, supportive oncology and survivorship.

This Advanced Integrated Science Course is a 4-week course that will take a multidisciplinary approach to obesity and its related complications. We will address physiologic, pathologic, psychologic, metabolic, genetic, nutritional, and social contributions to and consequences of obesity. We will discuss obesity-related comorbidities such as cardiovascular disease, obstructive sleep apnea, and type 2 diabetes. We will cover weight bias and stigma, and we will learn and practice motivational interviewing skills. We will also discuss current and potential diagnostic approaches and treatments for obesity. Clinical learning will include experiences at the Comprehensive Weight Management clinic and others. Lifestyle-related activities will include culinary medicine, food pharmacy tour, health coaching, exercise physiology, and registered dietitian experiences.

This Advanced Integrated Science Course will take a multidisciplinary approach to visualizing and understanding the complexities of the human body. Participants will conduct cadaveric dissections with focus on a particular body region: thorax, abdomen, pelvis and perineum, head and neck and limbs. Accompanying each dissection will be a focused and detailed study of the same region of anatomy using a variety of imaging modalities (x-ray, CT, MRI, US). Classroom related activities will synthesize structure and imaging through a variety of clinical cases. Non-classroom learning activities will include multiple clinics with radiologists.

This course is a 4-week examination of newborn care. The rotation will include two weeks of inpatient clinical time in the Well Baby & Intermediate Care Nurseries. Students will also experience continuity of care & the full spectrum of a newborn patient in their first weeks of life by participating in lactation consults & newborn follow-up clinic. Two weeks of non-clinical experiences will focus on nuances of newborn medicine. Newborn transitional physiology & the differences between term newborns & late preterm will be explored via team-based learning projects & the S.T.A.B.L.E. curriculum. We will discuss nutritional needs of newborns. Students will practice effective communication with parents to learn how times of family transition can impact well-being.

This course is a four-week basic science to bedside, deep examination of cardiovascular physiology, pathology and pharmacology. These complex topics require dedicated time to explore fundamentals. Cardiovascular disease is ubiquitous and understanding the basic science nuances and its application at the bedside is paramount for most physicians in their clinical practice. Students will sequentially analyze cardiovascular topics to facilitate an understanding of pathophysiology of cardiovascular disease and its impact on patients. The course will consist of flipped classroom didactics, problem-based learning, team-based learning, simulation activities, journal club, hands-on lab and a variety of clinical experiences.

This is a 4-week examination of the impact of toxicologic processes on patients in Utah. Students will be part of a multi-disciplinary team of ~8 people rotating at the Utah Poison Control Center. Students will follow patients managed by the UPCC in hospitals throughout the state for various toxicologic processes, then present daily at table rounds. Responsibilities include: researching types of poisonings/toxicologic processes to make recommendations for patient care, follow-up with care team members, communicating treatment recommendations & documenting patient status, presentations on toxicologic topics, journal club presentations, virtual attendance at regional/national case conferences, & optional submission of an abstract to 1 of 2 annual national conferences in Medical Toxicology.

This Advanced Integrated Science Course is a four-week deep examination of pandemic viruses and how they impact human health. The impacts of newly emerging viruses in healthcare and society are illustrated in dramatic detail in the long toll of the HIV pandemic going back to the 1980s and more recently in the COVID-19 pandemic. This course will cover the pathways by which viruses emerge to cause outbreaks in human populations; the mechanisms by which viruses propagate and cause disease; how therapeutics halt viral processes and are developed & evaluated; the role of social determinants of health in propagating healthcare inequities during viral outbreaks; and the modern medical approaches used to treat and prevent infections by pandemic viruses after they transition to endemicity.

This Advanced Integrated Science Course is a 4-week bench-to-bedside, deep examination of renal physiology, pathology & pharmacology. This course takes students through nephrology topics to facilitate an understanding of pathophysiology of acute & chronic kidney disease as well as the impact on patients. This course will combine lectures, case, team, & PBL sessions, lab time, journal clubs, & clinical experiences that will give students an in-depth look at what the kidneys do & how that translates to patient care. The 1st week will focus on fluid, electrolyte, & acid base regulation, the 2nd week on acute kidney injury, the 3rd on chronic kidney disease, & the 4th on kidney transplant & end stage renal disease. Each week, will have clinical/lab experiences to reinforce learning.

This course will introduce students to manual medicine modalities. The preliminary goal of the course will be to educate students regarding common manual medicine modalities (massage, acupuncture, and osteopathic manipulation) including history, principles of practice, treatment technique, and indications for treatment/referral. From this base, students will learn introductory steps in tissue palpation and diagnosis and will be guided in application of simple techniques to address common musculoskeletal conditions (headache, neck pain, back pain, sacral pain, SI joint pain). Movement and mindfulness techniques will be integrated with hands-on practice to develop internal/external listening. Finally, students will be offered an open session to ask questions and observe selected treatment approaches with the instructors. Through this elective, students will have the opportunity to explore various modalities and their application to musculoskeletal medicine and will be encourage to explore a modality of choice through shadowing or personal treatment experience. Please note that this elective will be comprised of 4-hour sessions over the course of 2 full days. Please assure that you will be able to attend all sessions when enrolling in this course.

This course serves as an introduction to health law for non-lawyers, aimed at health care professionals. It will cover crucial aspects of the U.S. healthcare legal framework, including major federal statutes affecting health care (such as Medicare, Medicaid, the ACA, EMTALA, ADA, HIPAA, and GINA). Additionally, the course will address regulatory and case law related to intellectual property, research, medical malpractice, non-discrimination, and the duty to treat. No previous legal coursework is required.

Many forms of art—visual, performance, cinematic, literary, etc.—portray aspects of medicine. In this course we will consider a wide range of artworks and art practices that represent figures or concepts related to medicine. We will also create our own art, exploring a variety of techniques and media. Questions we will consider together include: How do certain artworks explore artists’ relationships to medical practices as they experienced them? How does making or viewing art shape and enhance medical practice? Why and how is the term “art” used in discussions of medicine?

This course will employ multiple creative and reflective approaches to writing about medicine and about the experience of training to become a physician. A selection of literature—including prose (fiction and non-fiction), poetry, and memoir—will provide inspiration and instruction. Topics addressed in the course through written texts and assignments may include narrative medicine, histories of medicine, and the physician as author.

This 0.5 elective course invites medical students to explore their mode of authentic leadership, offering hands-on experiences that reveal the critical interplay between personal values, innate strengths, and refined self-awareness. Designed to empower future physicians, this course merges reflective exploration with practical exercises to cultivate leadership that is ethical, empathetic, and impactfulin complex healthcare environments. The course is structured around four leadership principles. It will consist of independent learning and reflection and four in-person, synchronous two-hour discussion sessions. Students will prepare for each session by reading high-yield articles and completing leadership and personality type indicator tests. Following each seminar, students will write a short reflection on how they are applying the newly learned principles to their leadership roles and provide an oral presentation on what they have learned.

This course introduces various bioethical issues and dilemmas that arise in clinical practice. It will cover key topics, including informed consent, advance directives, futility and non-beneficial treatment, organ donation, and medical aid in dying. By identifying and analyzing ethical issues, students will develop strategies and ideas to help address these challenges when they arise in clinical practice.

In this course, students will take charge of their education through self-reflection and goal setting. Learning community coaches collaborate with each student, guiding them to identify their strengths, areas for growth, and individual learning preferences. The Individualized Learning Plans (ILP) serve as roadmaps, enabling each student to achieve competency in program objectives through a personalized approach to growth and development.  This course is required for all students in all 4 years of the MD program.

In order to teach the skills required to be a successful independent scientist this course will teach students critical thinking strategies for successful research. This will include how to digest and analyze papers and problem solve, both of which will review and apply material from core coursers. The instructors will develop specific course content. Topics may include: How to read a paper (read at home, discuss in class); Survey of the core services; Problem solving with open-ended problems posed on real-life or made-up situations. A focused effort will be made to help students identify topics that they can develop into grants in the Spring term. Grading will be based on participation and individual work.

description: To prepare students for their thesis research, prelims, and qualifying exams, we will offer a guided proposal preparation course in the second half of the Spring semester that builds on their experience earlier in the semester (critical thinking in research, reading of primary literature and problem solving). The guided proposal writing course will provide an opportunity for students to create an original research proposal by critical review of other grants, training in hypothesis generation, scientific writing, and experimental design. The written original grant proposal will be used as a basis for an oral qualifying examination by a faculty committee.

Ray Bradbury was a hard-working and prolific American writer whose stories and essays are full of creative insight. Through his writing and essays, you'll find a remarkable trove of wisdom. Join an award-winning local writer to deconstruct these works, explore Bradbury's process, and uncover every gem from the mines of this true American treasure.

One of the master stylists of the American novel, Edith Wharton writes of the "Gilded Age" with a sharp, ironic eye. Her tone-perfect novels of manners are rich explorations of the issues of class, sex, and freedom in upper class New York society in the late nineteenth and early twentieth century. They remain compelling reading--and perhaps even freshly timely in our new, ersatz Gilded Age. Please read each novel before our discussions.

Mermaid legends exist in every corner of the world--from seductive sirens of the Mediterranean to protective water spirits of West Africa and playful seafolk of the Arctic. In this course, we'll explore global tales and examine the symbolic roles mermaids have played across cultures, customs, and centuries. Through lively discussion, we'll dive into storytelling, history, and pop culture to uncover how these mythical beings have evolved over time--and why they continue to enchant us today. This class explores adult themes, language, and content.

Join us for a unique poetry workshop designed to inspire self-discovery and new ideas. Through guided prompts, you'll explore fresh content and forms, pushing creative boundaries while dedicating most of your time to writing. After brief introductions and goal setting, dive into a series of prompts that spark exploration and unlock new ways of thinking. Optional sharing will round out the session and you'll leave with a fresh body of work and prompts to tackle future creative blocks.

How do we tell stories? What do we include in writing, and what remains unsaid? Build your voice as we focus on a group of specific techniques for shaping and informing your creative skills including character, plot, point of view, description, dialogue, and setting. You'll read short selections of writing to see what techniques to beg, borrow, or steal. You'll experiment with writing exercises and read and discuss each other's work. Writing can be inventive, illogical, chaotic, and wonderful. You'll practice seeing the world in new ways and then recreate that experience on the page. This class explores adult themes, language, and content.

Taught in a workshop format, this course will get your creative juices flowing as we expand on topics covered in Creative Writing I--voice, tone, point of view, and use of tense along with journeying into literary elements such as metaphor and simile, symbolism, structure, and others. This class is a fun way to build and develop the skills in an encouraging and supportive environment. Come prepared to read, write, and talk. This class may explore adult themes, language, and content.

Join an award-winning screenwriter as he takes you through the steps of writing your own screenplay. Learn the form and structure of screenplays that sell in addition to best practices to help you avoid the pitfalls that often trap new screenwriters.

Journaling has become productivity's new darling. We'll explore beyond the hype and learn how and why journaling can be a fulfilling practice. Take a look at how different types of journals meet different needs, as well as how journaling can help with goal-setting, becoming unblocked, time management, creativity, and searching for inner peace. Let's make a record of the incredible adventures of our lives.

Join an award-winning author in this intensive writing workshop as you're guided through several exercises to generate ideas for your short stories. By the end of class, you'll have a piece of flash fiction ready to submit to publications.

Join a published author as he shares his discoveries in Eastern philosophy and their applications to the life of a writer. We'll focus on overcoming writer's block, the nature of the Muse, and the nature of the work. This is a class about wellness and art, philosophy and creation, work, success, and existence. Sessions include directed mindfulness meditations, lectures on basic Buddhist concepts, and explorations of how these can be successfully applied to the author's journey. You'll experience creative writing, discussions, homework, and camaraderie.

All experiences in life, no matter how small or seemingly inconsequential, are stories waiting to be told. One way a person can tell these stories is through the memoir--taking life experiences and turning them into narratives. Join us to learn about the memoir genre, read and write to explore it, and discover how to create a narrative that represents a time or theme in your life. There will be opportunities for discussion, reading, practice writing your own memoir, and workshopping  with your newfound writing community. All writing levels are welcome!

Whether you're just starting out or have been on the scene for awhile, digital marketing is a necessary part of every writer's and artist's professional life-but tackling it on your own can be overwhelming. Join us to learn tips and tools that will get you started building your online presence including ways to develop your brand, identify your audience, and use your online platform to add to, rather than detract from, your writing, art, or performances.

Take your pickleball game to the next level! Designed for players who already know the basics, this session focuses on refining your technique and developing stronger court strategy. You'll work on shot placement, consistency, and advanced skills such as third-shot drops, lobs, and directional volleys. Through focused drills and guided play, you'll improve your reaction time, movement, and decision-making on the court. By the end, you'll feel more confident and competitive in recreational games and ready to step up your play in leagues or tournaments.

Stride and glide your way into the perfect sport for exploring winter: cross-country skiing! You'll learn how to travel smoothly across low-angle terrain, then progress confidently to groomed trails, understanding the techniques that make movement efficient and enjoyable. We'll also cover the basics of ski and boot construction--so you can choose and care for your gear wisely--and practice how to use poles, bindings, and layers effectively for comfort and control in varying snow conditions. No experience needed; just bring your curiosity and energy for winter adventure!

We're living in a board game renaissance! The game options available to players today are unlimited-- strategy, party, war, engine-building, trick-taking, deck-building--the list goes on and on. But what do those terms even mean and which will you (and your family and friends) enjoy? This course is an exploration of the variety that exists in modern board gaming. Each class you'll learn and play a new board game that exemplifies a different style of game. Along with the featured game, you'll be given a list of games with similar mechanics to broaden your knowledge and provide you with more games to explore. You can expect to leave with new social connections, knowledge of new games you can play with your family and friends, and an appreciation for modern board game design.

Learn how to travel with intention, mindfulness, and ease. In this course, you'll explore how to design meaningful journeys that align with your values and passions, without over-planning or overpacking. Discover how to pack light (just one bag!), stay on budget, and avoid travel FOMO by embracing presence and spontaneity. We'll cover minimalist packing strategies, budget-savvy tips, and ways to connect authentically with people and places. You'll also explore platforms that help you meet like-minded travelers and create deeper connections on the road. By the end, you'll walk away with a personalized toolkit for traveling lighter, smarter, and more meaningfully--ready to take on your next adventure with confidence and clarity.

This course will deepen your understanding of essential chess concepts through structured lessons, guided practice, and dynamic gameplay. Explore tactical patterns, opening principles, strategic middle-game ideas, and critical endgame techniques that will help you think several moves ahead. Each session combines instruction with interactive exercises and game play, giving you the chance to test your skills against fellow students in a supportive, competitive setting. Whether you're aiming for tournament play or just want to sharpen your strategic edge, this class offers the tools and insights to elevate your game.

Get ready to unlock your inner archer! This comprehensive course is your gateway to the thrilling world of Olympic recurve archery. In this beginner-friendly course, you'll learn the fundamentals of this timeless sport, from technique and body alignment to safety and range etiquette. Build focus, balance, and confidence as you develop your skills alongside a welcoming community of fellow beginners. Along the way, you'll also explore the fascinating history behind archery's lasting appeal. No experience necessary; come ready to learn, have fun, and aim for the bullseye! Co-sponsored with Salt City Swords Fencing Club.

Discover the fun and fast-paced world of pickleball in this beginner-friendly class! Perfect for newcomers, this session will teach you the fundamentals of the game including rules, scoring, and essential techniques like serving, volleys, and dinking. You'll also learn proper court positioning and strategy, helping you build confidence and improve your skills while having a great time on the court. With hands-on coaching and practice drills, this class will prepare you to jump into recreational games or leagues with ease.

Explore the gentle, flowing movements of Contemporary Tai Chi in this introductory class. Designed for all levels, this course blends mindful breathing exercises with slow, deliberate motions to enhance balance, flexibility, and relaxation. While rooted in traditional Eastern practices, the class focuses on accessible health preservation techniques rather than specific Tai Chi styles, ensuring clarity for those unfamiliar with its diversity. Whether you're looking to reduce stress, boost your overall health, or discover a calming exercise, this course offers a peaceful connection to your body and mind. No prior experience is needed-just wear comfortable clothing and move at your own pace.

Join us to discover one of the fastest sports in the world: fencing with sabers. Not only will you acquire footwork and blade work, you'll also discover the history, rules, and etiquette of this fantastic sport. By honing your fencing skills, you'll improve your physical fitness, mental acuity, coordination, and balance. By the end of class, you'll have new skills, new knowledge, and a new community of friends.

Step into Utah's winter wonderland on this moonlit snowshoe adventure. Guided by the soft glow of a full moon and headlamps, you'll trek through peaceful, snow-covered trails while admiring the stillness and beauty of nature at night. All you need to bring is a sense of adventure, boots, and layers to stay cozy; we'll provide snowshoes, warm drinks, and plenty of good company. Whether you're new to snowshoeing or a seasoned explorer, this is a magical way to experience the outdoors in a whole new light.

This course is designed with the beginning hobbyist or mechanic in mind and will cover basic maintenance, from repairing a flat tire to tightening your headset. We'll discuss using tubes versus going tubeless, the correct tire pressure to run on your bike, and how to set up your bike to make riding as safe and comfortable as possible. We'll also cover derailleur indexing and tips to keep your bike shifting perfectly. Finally, we'll discuss emergency trailside maintenance, the best tools to carry for trailside repairs, and different strategies to get your bike home if something breaks on the trail.

We love to watch outdoor survival shows, but would you know what to do if you were left alone in the wilderness? Join us to learn what it takes to survive in the outdoors, including how to build various shelters using only a tarp and twine, starting a fire without matches, and various methods of water filtration. Your instructor--a wilderness first responder who has logged 10,000+ miles of backpacking and 400+ field days as a wilderness guide--will answer all your questions and share the essential items you should always keep handy. With your newfound skills, you can venture outdoors with the confidence of knowing you're fully prepared!

Skateboarding can feel intimidating at first, but at All Together Skatepark, we're all about supporting beginners--and anyone looking to build their skills. Whether you're stepping on a board for the first time or picking it back up after a break, our experienced instructors meet you where you're at. You'll learn the fundamentals, pushing, turning, stopping, and how to fall safely to avoid injury. Come face your fears, push past the nerves, and discover how fun skateboarding can be.

Master the fundamental chess principles, including piece movements, check, checkmate, and stalemate. You'll explore checkmating patterns, opening strategies, and crucial middle-game and endgame tactics. Finally, you'll learn how to compete confidently in tournament-style chess games. Whether you're just starting out or dusting off some old skills, this course will keep you motivated and prepared to take your game to the next level.

Join us and explore the migratory journeys of Black American people into Utah. From the era of Mexican Territory through the formation of Utah Territory and into statehood, you'll learn about the myriad pathways that brought Black individuals and communities to The Beehive State. You'll walk away with a new understanding of how Utah's Black history has shaped Utah's cultural and historical landscape.

Visit the largest municipal cemetery in the United States: The Salt Lake City Cemetery. The cemetery is 250 acres of beauty with historically and visually interesting headstones. We'll wander among the graves of the famous and infamous as we discuss the development of the land, the challenges it has faced over the years, who died when and how, headstone symbols, burial customs, and more. Please come prepared to walk up and down inclines and move over uneven ground.

View Utah's wild horses in their natural habitat with the Onaqui Catalogue Foundation. You'll learn about Utah's most iconic wild horse herd and how community-based citizen science is being used to document and share information about individual horses, behavior, social structures, foal births, and herd management. We'll start with a two-hour classroom session then, on Saturday, we'll meet at the entrance of the Onaqui Herd Management Area (HMA) located near Dugway, on a quest to observe and catalogue the horses in the wild. The following session we'll meet online to share photos and video and discuss what we saw in the field.

Thanks in large part to South Salt Lake's Mural Fest, our city has blossomed into an outdoor gallery of exciting murals by local and international artists. What better way to experience this creative explosion than a walking tour to visit the murals of the Creative Industries Zone? You'll join one of the organizers of Mural Fest to learn about the mural process, including how artists are selected, the techniques they use to paint large-scale works, and fun facts about key muralists. Then chat with the artists themselves and watch as they create their own murals. There's so much more to it than just painting walls!

The history of Salt Lake City can be weird, heartbreaking, and surprising. Join us to learn about the unseen history of our beautiful city by exploring the places and lives of everyday people at the turn of the last century. In this course, we'll focus on two neighborhoods that illustrate the economic and racial diversity of our city's past.

Explore one of Utah's great mysteries: the ancient Anasazi (Ancestral Puebloan) villages of Hovenweep. Located in the Four Corners region of southeastern Utah, these villages were built and occupied between 500 AD and 1280 AD, at which time the 35,000 Ancient Puebloans residing in the four-corners region mysteriously and abruptly abandoned their villages. Join a local enthusiast to discuss the culture of the ancient people who called this area home and explore via photographs the amazing architectural remains of the incredible stone structures-most with multiple levels!-of the Hovenweep villages.

Build on the skills you learned in our introductory ASL class by increasing your basic understanding of the language while further exploring culture and grammar. You'll develop and expand your vocabulary, rules of syntax, and knowledge of Deaf history. Together, we'll practice story-telling and gain exposure to the interpreter pathway.

Ready to take your Spanish to the next level? This low-intermediate course is perfect for students who have some Spanish experience and are comfortable using the preterite tense (speaking in the past). In this interactive and flexible class, you'll practice speaking with others while diving into cultural readings, short videos, and real-world topics from across the Spanish-speaking world. The class is shaped by the group--students are encouraged to get to know one another, support each other's learning, and grow together through shared conversation. Listening activities may be added depending on group level, and your instructor will provide grammar and vocabulary guidance as needed to keep your Spanish strong and progressing. Be ready to engage with a wide range of Spanish abilities, step out of your comfort zone, and try something new. Whether you're polishing what you know or pushing your skills further, this fast-paced and fun environment is the perfect place to stretch your skills and build confidence.

In this engaging continuation of Spanish I, you'll review key grammar concepts like present tense and stem-changing verbs while learning to express your wishes, likes, and dislikes. Expand your vocabulary, practice new sentence structures, and gain confidence discussing people, things, and actions in Spanish. Through fun speaking, listening, and writing activities, plus a touch of cultural exploration, our instructor will guide you in a supportive environment tailored to your progress. By the end of the course, you'll be ready to dive deeper into the language you love and even get a glimpse of the past tense!

Discover the basics of American Sign Language (ASL) in this engaging introductory course. Build a foundation for conversational signing as you explore sentence structure, grammar, numbers, the alphabet, and essential vocabulary categories such as food, colors, daily activities, and more. Through storytelling and interactive activities, you'll develop expressive and receptive communication skills while gaining cultural insights. By the end of the course, you'll be able to hold a full conversation using a blend of signing, fingerspelling, and cultural knowledge.

Elevate your Spanish skills in this dynamic conversation class designed for real-life application! In a welcoming and supportive environment, you'll practice your vocabulary and grammar alongside fellow students, all while discovering new terms and refining your language skills. Our instructor will tailor discussions to match your experience and proficiency, ensuring a personalized learning experience. Join us to deepen your understanding, explore topics that excite you, and gain the confidence you need to engage in Spanish conversation!

Learn the language of warmth and passion. We'll cover the basic conversational skills you'll need to travel to Italy while learning about the people, art, and culture of this fabulous country. This class is designed to be repeated as often as you wish.

Learning the basics of the language and customs of any foreign country is a great start to your vacation abroad. Gain an understanding of essential Japanese words and phrases to make your travels to Japan more pleasurable. We'll cover the common greetings, vocabulary, and Kanji necessary for navigating Japan, purchasing a train ticket, and ordering sushi. We'll also spend time learning about the unique culture and customs of Japan.

Have fun while learning the language spoken by more than 150 million people worldwide. You'll start by learning basic sounds and pronunciation, then learn how to count and tell time. You'll get to know a little bit about German culture and cuisine, then finally pick up some useful idioms while enhancing your vocabulary. Taught by a native German-speaking instructor, this class will be filled to the brim with examples of contemporary conversation and culture.

Have even more fun while learning the language that 150 million people in the world speak. You'll acquire basic language skills including vocabulary and conjugation as you focus on jobs, shopping, and making small talk. Finally, have some fun while learning how to communicate in German on the telephone. Taught by a native German-speaking instructor, this class will be filled to the brim with examples of contemporary conversation and culture.

Dive into your exploration of the Spanish language in a comfortable and safe environment with this beginning-level class. You'll learn about vocabulary, grammar, and culture of the Spanish-speaking world while practicing your reading, writing, listening, and speaking skills. You'll enjoy a relaxing and informative atmosphere as we cover topics including travel, education, technology, transportation, and more! Participate in lessons, games, activities, and conversations while you learn to tell time, ask and answer basic questions, use verbs in the present tense, talk about what you're currently doing, and describe yourself and others.

Create a stunning glass bowl or plate using transparent and opal glass in your own color palette. In this beginner-friendly, one-day workshop, you'll learn to cut glass and explore its chemistry, firing temperatures, and behavior under heat. Projects will be fired in a kiln (50-hour process) and available for pickup later.

Discover the joy of glass design as you create a stunning art piece from glass. You'll start the first day by making your own custom design sheets using techniques that incorporate glass powders, stringers, frit, and various reactions. On the second day, you'll transform the artist sheets into a unique glass object that features its own set of custom sheet designs.

There's nothing quite as delightful in the summer as basking outdoors with a refreshing beverage in hand. The sensation of a chilled glass with droplets of condensation gracefully gliding down its surface accompanied by the alluring sound of clinking ice cubes is simply irresistible. Whether one's preference leans towards gin or lemonade, iced tea or mixed drink, the addition of a handmade drink stirrer will undoubtedly elevate the drinking experience. Your finished product is four colorful drink stirrers that you can gift or keep all for yourself.

Woodturning is one of the oldest forms of woodworking--dating back over 3,000 years to ancient Egypt! Start your own journey into the world of woodturning as your expert instructor guides you through the essentials of lathe operation, tool mastery, and turning techniques. You'll shape spindles, craft custom pens, turn beautifully balanced bowls, and create lidded boxes with snug, friction-fit lids while learning the secrets of wood grain, sharpening, and finishing that bring each piece to life. Your class includes live demos, expert guidance, and plenty of time at the lathe. Whether you're aiming for artistry or utility, you'll leave this course with functional pieces of art you can enjoy for years to come.

In this heartfelt fused glass class, you'll create nine 2"x2" glass hearts using a heart-shaped mold, playing with color, texture, and layering techniques to bring captivating depth to each unique piece. Once fired, these little hearts can take on many lives: tuck them in your pocket as tokens of love, scatter them in bowls or on tables as charming accents, or turn them into magnets for a playful pop on your fridge or message board. Perfect for beginners and seasoned crafters alike, this class offers a creative, meaningful way to express what's in your heart--quite literally--in glass.

Give new life to beloved fragments in this thoughtful jewelry-making class inspired by the Japanese art of kintsugi. Using modern materials like epoxy and putty you'll transform broken or missing pieces--stones, gems, heirloom parts--into wearable works of art. Guided by the philosophy of honoring imperfections, you'll create a one-of-a-kind piece that tells a story of resilience and beauty. Bring your own cherished items to incorporate, and leave with a deeper connection to your materials, your memories, and the art of repair.

Give your old clothes a new story with hand embroidery! In this two-part workshop, you'll learn beginner-friendly embroidery techniques to upcycle garments with a creative flair. Perfect for total beginners or those looking to refresh their skills, this class will cover essential stitches, design transfer methods, and tips for making your embroidery last. Students can bring a piece of clothing or choose to use what our instructor provides.

Papermaking is a versatile and texture-rich craft. Join us for this unique process that uses simple, inexpensive tools to create something unique. You'll start with the basics of processing, forming, and adding finishing touches in the papermaking process. Then you'll dive into the vibrant world of pulp painting, using richly dyed paper pulp to craft colorful designs, textures, and layered patterns. It's a creative, hands-on process--and a whole lot of fun!

Construct a glass panel from beginning to end using the copper foil method. You'll learn to shape the colored sheets of glass by cutting, grinding, and wrapping each piece with copper foil to prepare for solder. Finally, you'll solder the glass together into a finished stained glass panel that you can hang and enjoy for years to come!

Discover the art of inkle weaving, a simple, satisfying technique for creating tightly woven bands with bold patterns. In this hands-on afternoon workshop, you'll learn how to warp an inkle loom and weave your own custom design. Whether you go for bright colors or earthy tones, you'll leave with a one-of-a-kind band that's perfect as a wrist strap, key fob, or wallet accent. No experience needed; just bring your curiosity and a love for handmade craft.

Create your own washable cotton placemats using a rigid heddle loom. We'll use a weaving pattern called "Log Cabin" in colors of your choosing. These beautiful mats make the perfect summer decoration or gift!

Discover how to create your own 3D metal jellyfish! You'll start by learning basic shaping and texture techniques utilizing various metalsmithing tools. Then, you'll review soldering techniques while learning new methods of assembly. Finally, you'll clean and polish your unique piece to achieve a finished look. These gorgeous jellyfish work great as ornaments, jewelry, or even as a fabulous art display. So join the fun and impress all your friends with your own handmade smack of jellies!

Glass in the sunshine is stunning, to say the least, and doubly-so when it's in your own yard. Join us and explore how to create your own unique variation of rectangle yard art. You'll learn how to score and cut glass into strips, the chemistry of glass, firing temperatures, and how glass behaves under heat. This is a one-day class; you'll pick up project at a later date.

Transform your quilt top into a beautiful finished quilt! You'll learn multiple basting techniques to secure the top to batting and backing, how to do straight-line quilting on your own sewing machine, and how to make and apply binding to finish your project. Whether this is your first quilt or your tenth, you'll leave with new skills and a community of creative friends.

A good tote is a practical and stylish accessory that can be used in countless ways. Join us to create the tote of your dreams! You'll learn basic bag-making skills like construction, inserting snaps and zippers, and creating handles. Then you'll beautify and personalize your design by making pockets and lining. Now when you head to the market, you can enjoy the inevitable compliments and say, "Thanks, I made it myself!"

Dive into the techniques and skills of ceramic under glazing and surface design in this one-session workshop. Using pre-thrown and prepared ceramic pieces, you'll explore mishima (fine, intricate design work), sgraffito (etching into pottery), and under glaze (colored painting), to create beautifully unique ceramic pieces. This class is perfect for everyone from the ceramic-curious to the experienced thrower.

Explore the fundamentals of metalsmithing and become familiar with the basic tools used in this craft. You'll learn the properties of different metals while experiencing annealing and basic sawing, soldering, and finishing skills. You'll leave this class with a simple ring or pendant in the metal of your choice. Students can expect to spend another $20-$50 in class on materials. All levels are welcome; no prior experience is required.

Have you ever wanted to work with metal for an art project but didn't know where to begin? Under the guidance of a welding expert, you'll get hands-on experience working with the equipment, metal, and different designs. Build your basic knowledge of welding while completing a project of your choice!

You bought the sewing machine, you watched the YouTube videos, but now you just need someone who can answer your questions and give personal guidance. This class is for you! Join us and gain confidence in sewing while you become acquainted with your machine. You'll learn about a variety of fabrics and construction techniques, how fabrics are used in various projects, the use of notions, and how to set a zipper. This class is intended for people who are brand new to their sewing machines.

Blacksmithing in the modern world is rooted in creating art and tools with fire and force. This is a beginner class designed to give you a taste of what being a blacksmith is all about as you use both contemporary and antique equipment to learn the ancient skill of forging steel with hammer and anvil. You'll learn hammer control, the different parts and ways to strike an anvil, and how to use them to maximize your effort. All class projects are designed to use the skills you develop to enhance your capabilities.

Crochet is a versatile handicraft that expresses your creativity, from blankets to stuffed toys; sweaters to decor. Join us to learn the basics of crochet and gain the skillset and knowledge to plan your own projects. Stick with the curriculum--suggested dish cloth and a scarf--or be adventurous and find patterns that speak to you. Together, we'll focus on simple stitches, color changing, yarn basics, and how to read a pattern.

Learn how to design and weave your own colorful seed bead earrings from a local Utah artist. Using the brick stitch method (a fundamental weaving technique to make earrings using glass seed beads), you'll dive in by creating your own simple design on paper, then weaving that design using thread and beads. Patience is key in this art form, but your time and effort will be rewarded with a unique final product that will make you the envy of all your friends.

Build on the metalsmithing skills you have learned previously and create a ring or pendant with a set stone. You'll use hand tools, a flex shaft, and a soldering torch to create decorative embellishments, a bezel stone setting, and a bail for your pendant. You'll also learn more advanced finishing techniques to take your jewelry to the next level.

Join us to learn the basic skills of woodworking through two in-class building projects. This class starts at the very beginning, making it perfect for anyone brand new to woodworking. You'll learn about common hand tools such as a hammer, measuring tape, and level; power tools such as an impact driver, drill press, jointer, router, and four kinds of saw; the best tool to use for your desired outcome, and how to operate it all safely. You'll walk away from class with a hand-built charcuterie board and a step-stool, as well as the knowledge you need to continue making projects on your own!

Love the idea of knitting but don't know where to start? Join us for an introductory class that will teach you what you need to get going, including concepts and vocabulary, yarn basics, how to cast on and bind off, knit and purl stitches, basic pattern reading, and how to sew simple seams. You'll leave class with two easy but impressive projects that you can use as gifts or keep for yourself: a Bitty Bunny and a pair of fingerless mitts.

Join us for an introduction to pottery class where you'll learn how to make a set of nesting bowls. You'll learn basic throwing techniques like centering clay, shaping a bowl, and how to throw varying sizes of clay. As well as decorating your pieces and learning how to create a matching set. By the end of this class you'll have a set of four hand-made nesting bowls to take home. Please wear comfortable clothes you don't mind getting clay on. Co-sponsored with Workshop SLC.

Embroidery is a fun and meditative craft that offers you the chance to step away from the stress of life while creating magical works of art. You'll start by learning basic outline and decorative stitches with a stitch sampler. Gain knowledge of hoops, floss, tools, and fabric then see your work blossom as you utilize these tools to make your patterns into a finished work of art. Your creativity will soar as you learn to embrace mistakes, snags, and knots. All expertise are welcome, from beginners to those with more practice. There will be plenty of opportunities to learn new stitches, refine skills, and play within this relaxing yet productive art form.

Immerse yourself in the ancient art of kintsugi, the Japanese technique of repairing broken ceramics. In this transformative course, you'll learn to embrace the philosophy that imperfections are integral to beauty. Discover the delicate art of mending broken pottery with gold, silver, or other precious metals, transforming them into stunning works of art. Join us on this journey of restoration, where you'll not only repair ceramics but uncover a deeper appreciation for the beauty found within flaws.

Discover the art of ceramics as we guide you through each step of working with a throwing wheel. You'll master essential techniques from wedging clay to centering a piece, pulling walls, trimming, shaping, adding feet, and making handles. Dive into surface decorations as you practice waxing, glazing, and firing processes. By the end, you'll proudly take home small treasures like bowls and mugs, a larger bowl, and the skills to continue crafting more masterpieces. Unleash your inner potter today! Co-sponsored with Workshop SLC.

If you know the basics of your sewing machine and want to explore clothing construction, this class is for you! Learn how to use fabrics in various projects, master common seam techniques, install pockets, and read patterns. Build on your sewing knowledge with practical garment construction skills. Join us to create beautiful, custom-made clothing and enhance your sewing expertise. Students should already know how to operate their sewing machine.

Unveil the mesmerizing art of silversmithing in our hands-on class! Craft your own exquisite silver ring, adorned with a captivating cabochon stone. Dive into the creative process as you design and shape a one-of-a-kind silver masterpiece, tailored to your exact size and style preferences. Select from a diverse array of semi-precious cabochon stones and silver materials to fashion a ring that reflects your unique personality and aesthetic.

Create a stunning work of glass art using linear patterns and beautiful colors. You'll start by exploring the chemistry of glass, how to cut glass into stringers and rods, and how glass behaves under heat. By the end of this single-day class, your design will be ready to spend 50 hours in the kiln becoming a finished plate that you can show off to friends and family. This is a beginner class; no experience necessary.

Create your own piece of art glass, perfect for display or use. You'll use "frit" (bits of sheet glass) to add transparent and opal colors to a bowl form. Explore the chemistry of glass, how to place frit to create depth and texture, and how glass behaves under heat. By the end of this single-day class, your piece will be ready to spend 50 hours in the kiln, emerging as a 5" art glass bowl. Best of all, there's no glass-cutting required! This is a beginner class; no experience necessary.

course_name: Textured Glass in a Box Frame
description: Delight in the beauty of fused glass as you create textured glass artwork filled with overlapping colors. You'll use transparent colors in your choice of color gradient to create designs reminiscent of beach or sunset. Starting with a glass plate, you'll learn how to score and cut glass into strips then marvel at the science of glass, firing, and how glass reacts to heat. Your finished piece can be picked up at a later date after being fired in the kiln for a total of 50 hours! This course is designed with beginners in mind, no glass experience necessary.

Join us for a fun and fast-paced workshop with two stylish projects that employ an assortment of glass applications. You'll learn how to cut glass, the chemistry of fusing it, and how to program kilns--an oft-misunderstood process. You'll create your jewelry during a single class session then pick your projects up at a later date.

Papermaking is a versatile and texture-rich craft. The process uses simple, inexpensive and attainable tools to create a unique form. This class will start with the basics of local and natural fibers and weave its way through processing, forming, and the finishing touches in the papermaking process. Students will walk away knowing how to continue to explore papermaking techniques at home. This class is designed to not only pull sheets of paper, useful in itself, but also push the boundaries of papermaking as an artform. Students can look forward to enhancing their paper through the use of watermarks as well as embossing and embedding techniques.

Papermaking is a fascinating and versatile artform that combines craftsmanship and creative expression. Its potential as a medium is often underestimated. This class focuses on the Eastern style papermaking process. We'll explore the most ancient form of papermaking, the Amate, using the bark from a Mulberry Tree. Students will use those same fibers, using a different technique, to create striking yet delicate paper. This step-by-step class will begin with the most basic foundation of paper and finish with a product unique to the individual artist.

Join us in learning a traditional Japanese needlework technique that combines beauty and functionality. Originally developed as a method of mending and reinforcing fabric, sashiko has evolved into a celebrated decorative art form. In this hands-on course, you'll learn the foundational stitching techniques, explore traditional patterns, and create your own sashiko designs. You'll gain insights into the cultural significance of sashiko and its meditative, rhythmic stitching process. Whether you're interested in preserving a piece of fabric, embellishing clothing, or creating artful textiles, this class is perfect for beginners and those looking to expand their crafting skills.

Learn how to set a gorgeous cabochon gem stone into a one-of-a-kind pendant using wire weaving. Unlike traditional wire wrapping, wire weaving uses a thick base wire as a frame, allowing you to craft intricate, eye-catching patterns with finer wires. In this hands-on class, you'll learn what wire to choose, essential tools, various weaving techniques, stone framing, and making a bail--plus, tips for ensuring your piece is free of tool marks. You'll walk away with your stunning ready-to-wear pendant and the skills you need to continue creating unique jewelry masterpieces.

Design and craft your own stunning bouquet in this hands-on workshop featuring sola wood flowers, an eco-friendly and lasting alternative to traditional blooms. You'll learn essential techniques to soften and treat these unique flowers, making them pliable and perfect for arranging. Discover how to dye them in vibrant, custom colors and attach sturdy stems to create lifelike floral designs. With guidance on floral arrangement and the use of greenery, you'll craft a personalized bouquet that blends balance and beauty. Perfect for DIY enthusiasts, this class provides the skills and inspiration to create floral masterpieces that will stay beautiful for years to come.

Anyone can learn to draw! This class will encourage you to explore drawing through a variety of materials, methods, and philosophies. You'll become familiar with charcoal, ink, graphite, oil pastels, and even alternative drawing materials as you complete exercises and activities to help you see what's in front of you and set your vision down on paper. Gain confidence as you become acquainted with your own unique drawing style.

Watercolor is both approachable and endlessly captivating, offering opportunities for playful exploration and lifelong mastery. At times, it feels like the medium itself has a mind of its own, inviting you to collaborate rather than control. In this beginner-friendly course, you'll dive into the basics of color theory and color mixing through observation and hands-on practice. Discover essential watercolor techniques, from washes to layering, as you learn to harness the fluid, unpredictable beauty of this delicate and powerful medium. With an emphasis on observation, you'll develop your skills and confidence while creating vibrant, expressive works of art. Come "play in the water" and begin your journey into the enchanting world of watercolor!

Join us to explore the nuances and beauty of oil painting! If you have little to no experience with oil paint, or if you're looking for a refresher, this class is for you. We'll break down the entire process of painting with oil and learn concepts such as color theory, composition, value, and art history as it applies to your process. You'll also learn what materials are needed and how to get set up. You'll watch demonstrations of the techniques used to apply paint, then put those techniques into practice. Our exercises will become more complex each week, culminating with your choice of painting project to be completed by the end of the course. You'll receive individual attention and critique during each class and walk away with a finished piece and the skills and techniques you need to paint a variety of subjects.

Collage begins with collaboration--bringing together fragments to form something new. Learn a variety of basic techniques, materials, and tools for creating your own collage, from favorite adhesives to the best blade for any task, and then apply these skills to a collaborative creative game and art process. In this playful, four-hour workshop, you'll create "Exquisite Collages," inspired by the Surrealist game Exquisite Corpse. Each participant will work on a panel of a larger collage, guided only by the piece before theirs. The final reveal? A surprising, collective artwork full of movement and imagination. You'll leave with your starting panel--now transformed by others. This is a chance to think outside the box, connect with others, and create something bigger together.

AI is everywhere--but are you using it wisely? In this hands-on class, we'll explore where artificial intelligence shows up in daily life and how to make the most of it without falling into common traps. From writing emails and organizing schedules to building resumes and analyzing spreadsheets, you'll learn how to use AI tools to save time and spark creativity. We'll also cover the risks: how to spot AI-generated fakes, when not to use AI, and how to avoid common pitfalls. Expect practical tips, ethical conversations, and a little bit of fun as we learn how to stay smart--and safe--while using AI in everyday tasks.

Brighten your winter day with colorful flowers. You'll start with simple shapes then use flowing lines and flowing colors to create a cheerful composition. Surprise yourself with what you can draw and paint on your own watercolor journey. This class is great for all levels of experience. Participants are encouraged to bring a selection of reference photos or may use those provided by the instructor.

Have you ever tried to photograph a child, athlete, or pet in motion and ended up with a picture of a blurry blob? Getting a good action shot is uniquely challenging but we're here to help! You'll learn pro tips for capturing movement including how to adjust your camera settings, shooting techniques, and post-processing skills. Join us and discover how to take your photos from fuzzy to fabulous!

You know what you're looking at, but your hand just can't make it look right on the paper. Join us to learn the techniques that will help your hands draw what your eyes see. After a few class sessions learning the FUNdamentals, you'll find inspiration at the Natural History Museum of Utah. We'll utilize the PASS method (Proportion, Angles, Shape and Shading) to teach your hands how to translate exactly what your eyes see. You'll find that there is always more to look at and new marks to make. You'll learn in a positive, nonjudgemental atmosphere, and move at your own pace.

Take an in-depth look at megapixel counts, white balance, shutter speed, lens opening, and other digital camera functions while learning how to use them to your advantage. We'll cover traditional photographic imaging skills such as use of shutter speeds and lens openings, composition, and portraiture so you can spend more time making great images and less time editing them on your computer. You'll get the most out of this class if your camera features manual as well as automatic controls. Please bring your digital camera and manual to the first class.

Take an in-depth look at megapixel counts, white balance, shutter speed, lens opening, and other digital camera functions while learning how to use them to your advantage. We'll cover traditional photographic imaging skills such as use of shutter speeds and lens openings, composition, and portraiture so you can spend more time making great images and less time editing them on your computer. You'll get the most out of this class if your camera features manual as well as automatic controls. Please bring your digital camera and manual to the first class.

Have you mastered shutter speed, lens opening, and ISO? Want to explore the unique features of your digital camera such as white balance, contrast, HDR, resolution, RAW shooting, metering modes, and black and white? We'll use a combination of field and classroom sessions to make the most of the immediacy of digital feedback. Learn to understand and benefit from the unique controls your digital camera gives you. Work with an experienced photographer to achieve the goals you've been striving toward.

Discover the basics of color theory including temperature, value, and how color schemes create color harmony in your artwork. You'll create a color wheel and learn tinting, toning, and how to mix paints to match a specific color. This class is perfect for students working in oil, acrylic, and watercolor, as well as those in any discipline wanting to fine-tune their understanding and use of color.

Join a local artist and art educator to continue your exploration of the fundamental methods and techniques of oil painting. You'll deepen and expand your knowledge about conceptualizing and creating compositions, limited versus expanded pallete, further color theory concepts, broken color, and painting from life versus painting from a photograph. You'll learn via instructor demonstration, individual attention with feedback and instruction, and a positive atmosphere that promotes self-growth.

Learn how to capture breathtaking images of your adventures in the natural world during this workshop that introduces you to the skills and techniques used by professionals. Topics include exposure control and light metering, the principles of visual communication, the qualities of natural light, advanced digital techniques, and the philosophy and tradition of the artist in nature. You'll learn through slide-illustrated lectures and group discussions/critiques. This class is for photographers of all levels; no experience is required. Please come prepared with your own camera.

Create your own vibrant watercolor paints from the ground up. In this hands-on class, you'll learn how to combine pigment, binder, and other ingredients to craft a personalized set of six watercolor pans. Explore the art and science behind paint-making as you mix, mull, and test your own colors. Whether you're a seasoned artist or simply curious about the process, you'll walk away with a deeper understanding of your materials--and a handmade palette ready for your next masterpiece.

The creative possibilities of watercolor are limitless--and can also be a bit intimidating for beginners. Learn the very basics of watercolor with a method that narrows the parameters without sacrificing the creativity and artistry of the medium. We'll work in a series of 3s: drawing in 3 minutes using 3 colors; applying the paint with 3 techniques; working with 3 values of light; and then creating a painting start to finish in 3 steps.

A symbol of love, roses are gorgeous to paint. Celebrate love--for a partner, a child, a pet, or yourself!--this Valentine's Day by creating beautiful watercolor florals. After drawing and painting a single rose from a provided tracing or from your own reference, you'll also create a beautiful heart-shaped valentine. Whether you're a beginner or an experienced painter, this class will guide you through simple techniques to create heartfelt compositions that bloom with color. Share your love through your own watercolor art!

Demystify the process of depicting a realistic likeness. Through careful observation, we'll focus on the fundamental mechanics of blocking in the head and face, using essential techniques and concepts of the picture plane, measuring, proportion, line, positive and negative space, value, volume, basic anatomy, and composition. You'll work primarily in charcoal, as well as pastel, launching on an adventure that may become a lifetime pursuit.

With today's digital cameras, just about anyone can take a snapshot. But it takes more than the casual click of a button to create a compelling and artistic photographic image. While most photography classes focus on the technical aspects of photography, this class is all about the art of photography. Learn fundamental concepts of image design and composition, explore photographic styles, master your optics, develop better positioning and timing skills, and improve your post-processing. Move beyond the technical hassles and learn to think and see like a photographer. Please be prepared to use your own digital camera for simple homework assignments.

Also known as Copperplate, English Round Hand, or Engravers Script, this style of pointed pen calligraphy evolved from the French Ronde hand in the seventeenth century. Neat, legible, and swift in execution, this writing style is perfect for special cards and invitations, or for adding a special touch to everyday journal entries or lists.

Painting convincing realistic forms in any medium requires the ability to draw those forms. Drawing is the act of defining 3-D forms on a 2-D surface. Join us to learn strong foundational drawing skills so you will be able to build a painting on an accurate structure. You'll even learn to draw confidently with your brush. We delve into the study of geometric forms, establishing correct proportions and angles, line quality, gesture and perspective. All levels of experience are welcome. Anyone can learn to draw, as well as improve their skills.

Learn techniques, tools, and tricks to make beautiful, abstract compositions. Alcohol inks are acid-free, fast-drying, transparent, permanent inks that are available in many exciting, vivid colors. Plus, you're able to ink on plastic surfaces that often repel paint. Experiment with this unique medium while creating a frameable piece of art. This class is for everyone, no experience is required! Please wear clothes you won't mind getting ink on as it is permanent.

Explore the captivating world of Japanese culture and visual arts through sumi-e painting and calligraphy. In this immersive course, you'll delve into the expressive power of black ink, learning how to master sumi-e techniques to create stunning paintings with depth and shading reminiscent of watercolor. Additionally, you'll delve into the art of sho calligraphy, using a brush to write Japanese characters with elegance and precision. Embracing the essence of an object or idea, you'll explore the beauty of working loosely and capturing the soul of your subject. Journey into the rich traditions of sumi-e and calligraphy.

Geometric drawing has been around in various forms for centuries and in various cultures all over the world. Join a local artist to learn both the history and practice as you explore this form of drawing that ranges from perfectly simple to uniquely intricate! You'll start by using various tools to create perfect circles, triangles, squares, pentagons, hexagons, and more. You'll then use these shapes as a basis to create regular and semi-regular grids to build intricate tessellating patterns.

Adobe Lightroom is a powerful, yet easy-to-use editor that can turn ordinary photographs into eye-catching wall-hangers. You'll learn how to crop and frame, manipulate light and color, reduce noise and enhance details, apply special effects, correct optical deficiencies, and explore masking to enhance specific portions of your images. You'll also explore Lightroom's different versions to help you decide which is best for you.

Painting convincing realistic forms also requires the ability to see values -- the light as it hits the forms of your motif. Seeing values and painting them accurately is crucial and difficult. This lesson is the most important lesson you need to paint mood and atmosphere and dimension. Join us for a focused, fast, and fun class. Do not miss it!

Soft pastels are a dry, pure pigment that allows you to create colorful, expressive marks with beautiful soft effects. They can be used alone or with other media such as water. You'll start by learning value, color layering and other fun techniques. You'll also learn how to protect and frame these pieces. Then, in the last three classes, you'll bring an 8x10 reference photo as your instructor guides you through creating your own unique pastel masterpiece.

Anyone can take a snapshot with their phone, but what does it take to make a photograph worth framing? Join us to elevate your smartphone photography skills. You'll delve into the nuances that differentiate smartphone from traditional cameras and how those distinctions influence the final image. Optimize the capabilities of your phone camera, harnessing the power of its unique features while navigating its limitations. Master photographic fundamentals while gaining proficiency in composition, lighting, and more. Finally, you'll learn versatile shooting techniques to unlock the secrets for cityscapes, landscapes, portraits, and motion photos-all using just your smartphone!

Zentangle is a method of meditative art making using structured patterns or "tangles," that utilize "elemental" strokes: dots, lines, curves, and orbs. Join us to learn the basics and beyond as you grow from making simple to more complicated work. Each creation is personal and allows you to relax, increase hand-eye coordination, and connect with others in a creative and positive atmosphere. No previous art experience or skill is required. The amazing part comes at the end when all of the work is viewed together in a class "mosaic." Come be part of making beautiful things together.
